 Live .  26,929 viewing 26929 viewing Live page Updated 4 minutes ago Robert Pattinson says being cast as new James Bond is 'honour of a lifetime'
 Summary
 Robert Pattinson has been named as the new James Bond - watch as London's Piccadilly Circus shares the news 
 In a statement, the 40-year-old British actor says "to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime"
 Pattinson's career spans two decades - perhaps best known for playing vampire Edward Cullen in the Twilight films, he has also starred in Harry Potter and, more recently, Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey 
 Daniel Craig might not have been an A-lister when he was cast as Bond, but this time producers clearly wanted a bankable name, writes our entertainment reporter 
 Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight has been writing the script for the next film, with Dune's Denis Villeneuve to direct - what we do, and don't, know about the film 
 Who else was in the race to play Bond? See our list 
 Thanking those who auditioned, Villeneuve says "we were surrounded by extraordinary talent", adding Pattinson "brings a spirit that is completely new"
 Close form Share your reaction
 Get in touch Media caption, Watch: Footage from 2010 shows Pattinson being asked about playing Bond Live Reporting
 Edited by Kieran Kelly and Caitlin Doherty
 A villain, a leading lady, and a song: Much still up in the air about next film published at 18:32 GMT 18:32 GMT 
 Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Javier Bardem (R) starred opposite Daniel Craig as the villainous Raoul Silva in Skyfall
 So we have our next 007, but there are plenty more big announcements to come. 
 The Bond theme is almost as iconic as the role itself, and the likes of Adele, Madonna and Tina Turner have all recorded songs in the past. 
 While musicians like Raye, Lana Del Rey or Dua Lipa have been rumoured, we have no clue who'll be offered the gig. 
 We're also eagerly awaiting news of who might be Robert Pattinson's co-star. 
 Historically dubbed "the Bond girl", past leading female actors of the franchise - including Léa Seydoux, Naomie Harris and Monica Bellucci - have said they find the term outdated. 
 And lastly, the villain . When he was 007, Daniel Craig faced off Javier Bardem's Raoul Silva, Rami Malek's Lyutsifer Safin, and Christoph Waltz's Ernst Stavro Blofeld.

 Pattinson is a chameleon in his roles, says British Film Institute head published at 18:20 GMT 18:20 GMT 
 CEO of the British Film Institute (BFI) Ben Roberts says he's delighted with Robert Pattinson as Daniel Craig's replacement. 
 "He's a different kind of choice", Roberts tells BBC News, adding that because he's starred in so many famous franchises, "he comes to the table with a huge amount of baggage".
 But he adds that the "amazing thing about Robert Pattinson is his ability to be a chameleon in his roles".
 Pattinson has a "timeless spirit", Roberts says. "He has depths, he has the look of a haunted man, which I think plays very well into the James Bond persona."
 Roberts thinks that Pattinson's popularity with Gen Z audiences as well as other age groups would have been "really important to the producers and to Amazon" when casting the role.

 The six actors who have played cinema's most famous spy published at 18:12 GMT 18:12 GMT 
 After learning that Robert Pattinson will be the seventh actor to play 007, let's look back at the six who previously portrayed the iconic British spy in the main film franchise.
 Image source, Bettmann/Getty Images Image caption, Sean Connery (1962-67, 1971, 1983) was the first actor to play Bond in the franchise's film debut Dr No - he went on to appear as 007 in seven films
 Image source, Silver Screen Collection/Getty Images Image caption, George Lazenby (1969). The Australian actor was the second Bond, playing 007 in On Her Majesty's Secret Service
 Image source, Anwar Hussein/Getty Images Image caption, Roger Moore (1973-1985). He appeared in seven Bond films including Live and Let Die and A View to a Kill
 Image source, Keith Hamshere/Getty Images Image caption, Timothy Dalton (1987-89). He had two outings as Bond and was said to be more brooding than earlier portrayals
 Image source, Keith Hamshere/Getty Images Image caption, Pierce Brosnan (1995-2002). Brosnan starred in four Bond blockbusters, beginning with GoldenEye
 Image source, Eon productions via Press Association Image caption, Daniel Craig (2006-21). Played 007 in five films spanning 15 years - longer than any other actor. Depicted a more emotionally complex protagonist than in previous films

 Pattinson originally went to theatre school 'because a lot of pretty girls went there' published at 18:00 GMT 18:00 GMT 
 Helen Bushby 
Culture reporter 
 Image source, Getty Images Born in Barnes, south-west London, Pattinson grew up with his father, a classic car trader and mother, who worked at a modelling agency, and two elder sisters.
 His interest in acting started while he was still at school, when he joined the Barnes Theatre Club.
 "I went originally because a lot of pretty girls went there," he said. "I worked backstage and I started acting when all the good people left and I was the only one tall enough to play the lead.
 "In a weird sort of way, that stuff was probably the best I've done and the stuff I am most proud of."
 He landed his first big film role more than two decades ago, playing Cedric Diggory in 2005's Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire. A relatively minor character, but it was enough to get him noticed.
 Three years later, he had a starring role in the first of five Twilight films, along with Kristen Stewart, in which they played star-crossed lovers - vampire Edward Cullen and mortal-turned vampire Bella Swan.
 He's already established himself as a leading man, action star and character actor, which is clearly why he is about to play the suave, British secret agent 007.
 At 40, he is slightly older than some of the other men reportedly lined up for the role, but he's also the most famous - something the new Bond studio Amazon-MGM may have favoured, with an eye on the box office.

 Shaken or stirred? Your reactions to Pattinson as Bond published at 17:48 GMT 17:48 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images "Pattinson is suave, has good physicality, good looks, a definite screen presence, and can turn his features into a cold and aggressive stare at the drop of a hat," says Richard from Richmond . 
 But Mike from Liverpool says he would have preferred someone at "the start of their journey as Bond". 
 In South Yorkshire, Steve thinks Pattinson "is a great actor, so it should be great", but cautions that Daniel Craig left a "template" and "it's always hard to follow in successful footsteps".
 Justin from Yeovil thinks that Pattinson "really looks the part", but that he "just needs a few tomahawk steaks and chips to bulk up a bit".

 Peaky Blinders creator to pen Bond script published at 17:41 GMT 17:41 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images There is still lots we don't know about the next James Bond movie - but we do know who will be writing it: Steven Knight.
 Knight has been writing in the television industry since 1989, but is perhaps best known for creating the Peaky Blinders series, which first aired in 2013.
 The first movie he wrote, Gypsy Women, aired in 2001 - more recently wrote Peaky Blinders: The Immortal Man and Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger, both of which came out earlier this year.
 Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme in September, Knight said he was "doing my duty for King and country" by taking on the script. 
 He continued: "The thing with Bond is it’s its own universe, and it’s its own franchise. So there are certain rules. I mean, obviously you have to move it along, but I love where it sits. I love that it’s British."

 Bond actors never used to be megastars - intentionally published at 17:31 GMT 17:31 GMT 
 Regan Morris 
Reporting from Los Angeles 
 Image source, Reuters This is Amazon’s first Bond movie and Hollywood - as well as Silicon Valley - do things quite differently from the Broccoli family who controlled the 007 franchise for more than six decades.
 The Broccolis handpicked every Bond actor. They were never megastars - intentionally. The actor was never meant to eclipse the character.
 That’s not how Hollywood rolls. Always risk averse with huge budgets at stake, Hollywood banks on celebrity so people here are not surprised by Robert Pattinson.
 Prominent Hollywood journalist Matthew Belloni predicted Pattinson would be cast as Bond last week, stating he may be boring but he’s the obvious pick because he is a super star who’s already played Batman. 
 "Pattinson seems to me like the lowest-risk choice in an age of risk minimization," Belloni wrote in his newsletter.
 "Maybe he’s boring. Maybe Hollywood would be passing up a chance to anoint a badly needed new star. But with so much at stake for everyone involved, that all makes him the obvious pick."

 Pattinson previously told me 2026 was one of the best years of his life published at 17:26 GMT 17:26 GMT 
 Noor Nanji 
Culture correspondent 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Robert Pattinson appeared in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey earlier this year
 Robert Pattinson recently told me this has been “one of the best years of my life”.
 To be clear, the question I’d asked him was NOT about Bond – it was a question, at the premiere of his latest film Primetime, about whether this could be the year he gets his first ever Oscar nomination.
 "I am eternally grateful that I got these jobs," he told me.
 "But then [to have] been able to even do them, this is one of the best years of my life."
 That year has just gotten even better for him.

 It's been a bumper year for actor Robert Pattinson.
 He's starred in multiple box office hits - from Christopher Nolan's mythical epic The Odyssey, to Kristoffer Borgli's dark comedy The Drama. 
 He's graced the red carpet numerous times as a result - take a look in the short video below.

 Ian Fleming estate welcomes Pattinson to Bond family published at 17:17 GMT 17:17 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, British author Ian Fleming at his desk in 1958
 The estate of Ian Fleming - the writer of the original James Bond spy novels - and Ian Fleming Publications are "delighted to welcome Robert Pattinson to the James Bond family", they write in a post on X. 
 Fleming, who died in 1964, wrote 14 James Bond books during his career, the first of which was Casino Royale in 1953.
 "As Bond himself reflects at the end of Moonraker when facing the fact that the object of his affections is engaged to another man, 'He must play the role which she expected of him. The tough man of the world. The Secret Agent. The man who was only a silhouette,'" the official Ian Fleming account writes on X. 
 They add that they're excited for Pattinson to step into that silhouette and make it his own. 
 "We have no doubt that Ian Fleming would be amazed at the longevity of his creation and the fact that the world is still hungry for tales of the world’s greatest spy.​"

 We know who'll play the next Bond, but what about his love interest? published at 16:56 GMT 16:56 GMT 
 Noor Nanji 
Culture correspondent 
 No announcement has been made yet on who will get that part.
 Although I note that Robert Pattinson’s real-life partner Suki Waterhouse, a singer and actor, once said she’d love to play "a badass Bond girl", according to the Irish Mirror , external .
 It could be more likely that Waterhouse picks up a cameo role in the film, if indeed she wants one.
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Robert Pattinson is engaged to actor and singer Suki Waterhouse

 Why has the casting process taken so long? published at 16:51 GMT 16:51 GMT 
 Steven McIntosh 
Entertainment reporter 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Daniel Craig announced in 2019 that No Time to Die - released in 2021 - would be his last
 There are several reasons that it's taken five years since the release of Daniel Craig's final Bond film to find his replacement.
 Firstly, there have been a lot of changes behind the scenes - the previous Bond producers sold the franchise to Amazon MGM in early 2025, and it would've taken a while for a new creative team to settle in and decide on their strategy.
 The studio also prioritised appointing the director (Denis Villeneuve) and writer (Steven Knight) to set the tone of the next film, before turning to the question of which actor would be the best fit for their new era.
 Once those building blocks were in place, however, the casting process did not take long, and really ramped up in the last couple of months.
 Hollywood trade magazines have been packed with up-to-the-minute stories in recent weeks about when screen tests were taking place and which actors had dropped in and out of the race. 
 The long gap since Craig announced in 2019 that he'd be leaving the role has meant that previous favourites such as Tom Hardy and Idris Elba aged out of the role. But once the search was under way, it didn't take long for producers to land on Pattinson.

 Who else was in the race to be Bond? published at 16:44 GMT 16:44 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Jack Barton (L-R) are all thought to have been considered for the role
 A handful of actors were thought to have made it through to the final screen tests before Robert Pattinson, 40, ultimately bagged one of Britain's biggest film roles. 
 They included:
 Jack Lowden , 36, who plays the role of MI5 intelligence officer River Cartwright in the TV series Slow Horses.
 Josh O'Connor , 36, who portrayed Prince Charles in The Crown.
 Callum Turner , 36, who appeared in the Harry Potter prequel Fantastic Beasts and in The Capture as Shaun Emery.
 Jack O'Connell , 36, played the character of James in Skins and recently appeared as the vampire Remmick in Sinners.
 Nicholas Hoult , 36, also appeared in Skins at the beginning of his career, before going on to star as Lex Luthor in the recent Superman movie.
 Jack Barton , 31, recently played the role of David Nelson in Heartstopper.

 Pattinson gets Royal approval as 007 published at 16:37 GMT 16:37 GMT 
 Image source, Pool/Getty Images The official Instagram account for the Royal Family, which represents King Charles III, Queen Camilla and other working Royals, has shared its reaction to Robert Pattinson's casting as 007.
 Sharing the announcement, the page says: "Welcome to His Majesty's Secret Service, Mr Bond."

 Pattinson's career through the years - in pictures published at 16:28 GMT 16:28 GMT 
 Robert Pattinson has played a huge range of characters: an immortal being in Twilight, Batman, controversial TV presenter Chris Hansen, and many other notable roles. 
 Here's a look at Pattinson's career in pictures:

 Bond reveal comes 20 years after release of Casino Royale published at 16:15 GMT 16:15 GMT 
 Today's reveal comes 20 years after the release of Casino Royale - Daniel Craig's first film starring as 007.
 The 21st official Bond film had its world premiere on 14 November 2006 in London, and was then subsequently released in UK cinemas on 16 November.
 Craig played the role in five Bond films spanning 15 years.
 Media caption, Watch: What Daniel Craig said when he was cast as Bond in 2005

 What we do and don't know about the next Bond film published at 16:11 GMT 16:11 GMT 
 The next James Bond actor has finally been unveiled as Robert Pattinson - here's everything else we do and don't know about the next 007 film:
 We do know...
 The writer and director: Steven Knight will pen the script, while Denis Villeneuve will direct the film
 A rough date: the film is expected to go into production in 2027, before its release in 2028
 It will be the 26th film in the official series
 We still don't know...
 The name of the next film
 Its exact release date
 Which artist will be chosen to perform the Bond theme and title song
 Other actors in the cast, such as the villain

 New era of Bond unveiled on social media published at 16:05 GMT 16:05 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Robert Pattinson was revealed as 007 in a slick social media post featuring the actor dressed in a black tuxedo.
 A short video also shows the actor pointing a gun as he is surrounded by darkness.
 The words "James Bond will return" then follow.
 The announcement could not be more different to when Daniel Craig was revealed as the sixth Bond actor back in 2005.
 Craig arrived at a news conference in London on a Royal Marines speedboat, joking that he "had a couple of Martinis" after securing the role.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Robert Pattinson is a bankable movie star published at 15:55 GMT 15:55 GMT 
 Steven McIntosh 
Entertainment reporter 
 Image source, Getty Images One of the most interesting things about the choice of Robert Pattinson to play 007 is that he is an actor who already has significant profile.
 Many of the other contenders thought to have been in the race - such as Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O'Connor - might all be hot, up-and-coming actors, but none is truly a household name. 
 Pattinson, on the other hand, is a proper movie star, with a proven track record of box office success and ability to lead major franchises such as Twilight and The Batman. 
 Whatever your opinion on Pattinson, one thing for sure is that most audiences will have at least heard of him. 
 Daniel Craig might not have been an A-lister when he was cast as Bond, but this time producers clearly wanted a bankable name to lead the first iteration of Bond under Amazon's umbrella.
